difference.candidate_requirement: When a report database connection fails, the public API must return the stable error=reporting database unavailable value and must not expose SQL text, ORM aliases, driver details, backend topology, or internal exception strings. Status, zero counts, bounded completion, generation-guard release, and recovery behavior remain exact assertions.
difference.oracle_behavior: After the blocked report query loses its PostgreSQL connection, frozen Java returns HTTP 200 but copies a Hibernate/JDBC exception containing the full SELECT statement, generated table alias, driver I/O text, and [n/a] marker into the public error field.
difference.candidate_behavior: Rust returns HTTP 200 with the same date and zero counts but the fixed error=reporting database unavailable value. It does not expose SQL or driver internals.
difference.reason: Returning raw database exception text is an information disclosure and creates an unstable external contract tied to ORM and driver versions. The rewrite preserves the response shape while redacting implementation details.
difference.scope: Only the error string for report database failures. HTTP status, content type, exact candidate JSON bytes, counts, date, application continuity, database crash recovery, connection-pool recovery, retry success, and all side-effect assertions remain fixed. Healthy report behavior and timeout behavior are covered separately.

evidence.fault: SIGKILL the isolated PostgreSQL process group after pg_locks confirms the report query waits behind ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
oracle_disclosed_terms: An I/O error occurred while sending to the backend

contract.durability: Both isolated PostgreSQL clusters run with fsync=on, synchronous_commit=on, full_page_writes=on before the crash; the candidate fixture performs CHECKPOINT before application start.
contract.fault_admission: pg_locks must show exactly one ungranted AccessShareLock for inbound_dmarc_log before SIGKILL
contract.application_continuity: application PID unchanged across the database crash and recovery
contract.database_recovery: PostgreSQL restarts from the same data directory on the same port with a new PID
contract.outage_response: HTTP 200, zero counts, implementation-specific frozen error string
contract.retry_response: HTTP 200, zero counts, error=none without restarting the application
shared_side_effects: unchanged Redis pending queue while down and after recovery
unchanged Sent Maildir while down and after recovery
unchanged PostgreSQL source rows after recovery
explicitly_not_claimed: unclean crash during a committed write
